Speechley again showed that he is faster than ever, and Charlie Churcher and Redgrave also distinguished themselves. In fact, the performances of the three last-named, all "Juniors," were very encouraging, as were those of Rutland, already mentioned, and Storey.

Charlie Speechley, the holder, was favourite, and went to the front from the start, closely followed by Charlie Churcher. It seemed, at the half-distance, that we were to be robbed of the close race which had been promised between these twain, for Speechley had opened up what appeared to be a winnin…

Despite early setbacks in the shape of the disqualification of Charlie Churcher and Charlie Speechley, who had both been expected to be with the leaders, and later that of Wright, who was shown to be in the wrong, as previously mentioned, our remaining “A” team men stuck gamely to their task and had…

Speechley was 10th and Bidgood 18th (both walking in Polytechnic colours); whilst Rutland and Wright finished together in 20th position. The last-named two and Treacher walked as members of Cadogan A.C.

From the start Jack Field cut out the pace, opening up a distance of 50 yards in the first mile from Bentley, Bidgood, Harley, Martin, Speechley and Rickards, all of whom appeared unconcerned at the pace set by the leader.

In the next event, the 2 Miles, we were represented by Speechley and Harley, whilst Surrey W.C. had Fisher and Burgess, the Kent champion. From the start Stone (Poly.) led, followed by the Surrey pair, and our two.
A terrific struggle was expected between the holder, C. Speechley and our Captain, C.

Once again we have a likely lot of "Juniors" and from their numbers it should be possible to find a team capable of winning once again if only they will train steadily and regularly, and not spasmodically. Names that come to the mind are Speechley, Sutton, Storey, R.
The race was slightly marred by the absence of Bridger, Elliott and Speechley, whose presence would most certainly have made the race keener.
